card.title: 78th STEEL REGIMENT
card.text: Deployment: Gets +2+2 for each enemy unit in the frontline.
card.flavorText: The 78th Infantry Regiment was a unit of the 20th Infantry Division of the Polish Army which was formed in 1920. In the summer of 1939 it was part of the Modlin Army which was tasked with defending the area near the interwar border of Poland and East Prussia. Between September 1st and 3rd, 1939, during the September Campaign, the 20th Infantry Division defended positions in the Battle of Mława against the German I Army Corps, consisting of the 11th Infantry Division, 61st Infantry Division and the Panzer Division Kempf. The German forces failed in their first attacks and lost approximately 25 tanks. On September 2, the Germans tried and failed again, but subsequently they managed to organize a successful offensive and to break through Polish positions on September 3rd. An attempted counter-attack by the Polish 8th Infantry Division failed, resulting in a chaotic retreat. Given the challenging circumstances, the 20th Infantry Division was ordered to withdraw on the night of September 3rd. They were bombed by the Germans and reached the Płock area around September 7th, where remnants of the division entered Warsaw to participate in its defense. Finally the division surrendered along with the Warsaw garrison on September 28th.The German forces that faced the 20th Infantry Division at Mława nicknamed it the "Steel Division".
